body.statement: For \(\mathcal C_{n,m,\delta}^{\mathrm{exact}}\) at a prespecified \(\delta\), establish \(\Pr\{\Theta_{I,\delta}(b,q,\omega)\subseteq\mathcal C_{n,m,\delta}^{\mathrm{exact}}\}\geq1-\alpha\), conditional on realized treatment-arm sample sizes, for every law in \(\mathfrak M_\delta(b,q,\omega)\) and every external sampling law in the stated sampling model, including zero trial or exposure cells and extended zero-denominator branches. Derive a finite computational representation of the projected closed set that preserves empty candidate fibers and does not select an endpoint optimizer.
body.justification: Exact primitive-cell inversion makes whole-set coverage definite at zero counts and leaves only the nontrivial projection geometry to resolve.
body.gap: Romano and Shaikh (2010) give general whole-set coverage and Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019) give calibrated projection, but neither derives this finite exact multinomial projection through extended reciprocal common-history fibers.
body.consumer: Regulators obtain a finite-sample confidence statement for every compatible ratio value without asymptotic rate restrictions or ad hoc zero-cell corrections.
